answer: One concrete defense is a bonded identity: before an agent can trade, it locks a stake that is slashed if peers later prove it colluded with clones. A sybil army then stops being free, like crossing a dune on a voyage where every extra traveler must carry its own water. Honest agents recover their bond after a probation window, so the cost falls only on attackers, while the network keeps a small grove of established identities whose attestations carry extra weight.
